transcript.text: fridge part freezin stuff, lettuce + yoghurts frozen solid at the back. hotpoint ff. any ideas pls

That’s usually the fridge section getting too cold at the back — common causes are:

• Temperature set too cold: set fridge to around 3–5°C (or dial roughly middle, e.g. 3 of 5).
• Food touching the back wall: the cooling plate/air outlet is often at the rear, so keep lettuce, yoghurt etc. a few cm away from it. Use the front/middle shelves for easily frozen items.
• Blocked air vents: don’t pack food tightly around vents (often rear/top of fridge), as this can create a freezing cold spot.
• Door not sealing properly: check the rubber seal for gaps, dirt or damage. A poor seal can make the fridge run constantly.
• Ice/frost buildup: if there’s lots of frost or ice on the back panel, switch it off and fully defrost it (doors open, towels down; don’t chip ice off with a knife), then restart.

If it keeps freezing food even on a middle setting and with space at the back, likely possibilities are a faulty thermostat/temperature sensor, or on a frost-free model an air damper/control fault. That generally needs a Hotpoint/white-goods engineer.

For now, move anything that freezes easily away from the rear wall and check with a fridge thermometer if possible. If the fridge is consistently below about 1–2°C, it needs attention. If you can share the full Hotpoint model number (usually inside the fridge), I can narrow down the likely fault.
dial is on max, kids prob moved it. fridge is rammed after big shop and stuff is pushed against the back vents. model starts H8 but sticker's behind the salad drawer so cba emptying it

Yep, that’ll very likely be it.

1. Turn the dial down from MAX to the middle setting — usually 3 / “medium”.
   Give it 12–24 hours to settle; don’t expect an instant change.

2. Pull food away from the back wall/vents if you can. Even just make a small air gap — especially move the lettuce, yoghurts, milk, eggs and anything watery. Put less freeze-sensitive stuff at the back if you need the space.

3. Don’t block any obvious vents at the rear/top. A packed fridge is fine, but it needs some airflow.

4. If there’s a lot of ice on the back panel, a full defrost may be worthwhile — but first see whether changing it off MAX fixes it.

For a Hotpoint starting H8, MAX is often effectively “run colder/harder”, so food against the rear cooling area can easily freeze. You probably don’t need the exact model unless it continues freezing things after a day or two on a mid setting with the vents clear.
